chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Dermatology AI models are trained predominantly on light-skinned, cancer-focused image collections, yet are increasingly proposed for settings whose patients differ from the training population along two confounded axes: skin tone and disease distribution.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the research problem of decomposing the generalization gap in dermatology AI models into skin tone and disease-distribution shift effects.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: Linear probing: L2-regularized logistic regression is fitted on standardized frozen features using patient-level 70/30 splits to prevent leakage. Performance is reported as balanced accuracy. SCIN conditions are mapped into seven clinically grounded categories: inflammatory, infectious, vascular/purpuric, neoplastic, pigmentary, traumatic/other, and other.
chk_method.reason: The poster describes the evaluation methods, including linear probing, label-free representation quality analysis, and low-compute adaptation, matching the reference.

chk_data.label: accurate
chk_data.poster_evidence: HAM10000 + ISIC 2019: 35,346 images; source and in-domain reference. DDI: 656 images; tone-stratified evaluation using malignant/benign labels. SCIN: 6,517 images from 3,061 patients; tone-diverse, non-neoplastic distribution shift.
chk_data.reason: The poster lists the datasets used (HAM10000, ISIC 2019, DDI, SCIN) and their roles, matching the reference.

chk_setup.label: accurate
chk_setup.poster_evidence: Linear probing: L2-regularized logistic regression is fitted on standardized frozen features using patient-level 70/30 splits to prevent leakage. Representation quality: label-free k-nearest-neighbor purity is computed with k = 10 and cosine distance. Low-compute adaptation: SCIN performance is compared using a full linear probe, a few-shot probe with 10 examples per category averaged over five draws, and raw versus standardized features.
chk_setup.reason: The poster describes the evaluation protocol, including patient-level splits, kNN purity analysis, and few-shot adaptation, aligning with the reference.

chk_primary_result.label: accurate
chk_primary_result.reason: The poster reports the cancer baseline's balanced accuracy degradation from 0.62 in-domain to 0.21 on SCIN, matching the reference.

chk_secondary_result.label: accurate
chk_secondary_result.poster_evidence: SCIN purity lift: Cancer baseline: +0.06. DermLIP: +0.23. MONET: +0.14. DINOv3: +0.16.
chk_secondary_result.reason: The poster reports kNN neighbor-purity lift results, including DermLIP achieving +0.23 lift, consistent with the reference.

chk_baseline.label: accurate
chk_baseline.reason: The poster compares the cancer-trained baseline against dermatology foundation models and a general-purpose vision model, matching the reference.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: Disease-distribution shift dominated skin tone in the evaluated setting. Cancer-specialized features collapsed to near-chance structure on unfamiliar conditions, while dermatology-pretrained and broad general-purpose features transferred better.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster concludes that disease-distribution shift is the dominant driver of the generalization gap and highlights the benefits of dermatology foundation models, consistent with the reference.

chk_limitation.label: accurate
chk_limitation.poster_evidence: DDI and SCIN are US-sourced proxies, not cohorts collected in resource-constrained settings, so deployment-oriented conclusions are inferential.
chk_limitation.reason: The poster acknowledges that DDI and SCIN are proxies rather than genuine RCS cohorts, matching the reference's limitation.
